passages.original: Ἡ δ᾿ αἰτία, διʼ ἣν ἐπὶ τὸν ἀγῶνά τις ἀπήντηκε, σύστασιν ἔχει τοῦ πράγματος, ὡς ἐν τῷ κατὰ Νεαίρας· πολλὰ μὲν ἦν τὰ παρακαλοῦντα, ὧ Ἀθηναῖοι, γράψασθαι Νέαιραν τὴν γραφὴν ταυτηνί. ἡ γὰρ γνώμη σεμνοτέραν τὴν προκατάστασιν τοῦ λόγου ποιεῖ, ὡς ὁ Θουκυδίδης πανταχῆ.
passages.english: The cause on account of which someone has come forward to the contest establishes the matter, as in the speech Against Neaera: "Many things, men of Athens, were urging [me] to bring this indictment against Neaera." For a maxim makes the preliminary statement of the speech more dignified, as Thucydides [does] everywhere.
passages.notes: The quotation is the opening of [Demosthenes] 59, Against Neaera. The author is given only as a TLG number (0606), which I could not identify; the treatise is possibly the Ars rhetorica attributed to Rufus. The second sentence (on the maxim, gnōmē) seems to begin a new point, and may belong to a different heading. "Preliminary statement" renders prokatastasis, a technical term for the introductory exposition before the narrative.
